patterns.name: Service Connectivity Issues
investigation_steps: Verify Service selector matches Pod labels
Check if Pods are running and have assigned IPs
Verify container ports match Service target ports
Check for NetworkPolicies that might block traffic
Look for FAILED_CALL_TO or CALLS relationships to confirm network layer
For service mesh: Check VirtualService routing configuration
For service mesh: Verify DestinationRule policies
Distinguish between network-layer issues (no response) and application-layer issues (error responses)
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: Service connectivity failures typically manifest as connection refused, timeouts, or 503 errors. Follow the OSI model: verify network layer (DNS, selectors, endpoints) before investigating application layer. If you receive ANY error response (even 500 or gRPC errors), the network layer is working - focus on application issues. If you receive NO response, investigate network configuration (selectors, policies, routing).
recommendations: Fix Service selector to match Pod labels
Ensure Pods are in Running state with assigned IPs
Verify port configurations match between containers and Service
Review and adjust NetworkPolicy rules if blocking traffic
For service mesh: Fix VirtualService routing rules
Add monitoring for endpoint availability

patterns.name: Resource Exhaustion
investigation_steps: Check Pod events for OOMKilled or Evicted status
Spawn metrics investigation for memory, CPU, and disk usage
Examine resource requests and limits in Pod spec
Check Node capacity and current resource usage
Identify if this is a pod-level or node-level issue
Look for trends: sudden spike vs gradual increase
Check recent deployments that might have changed resource consumption
Verify if resource limits are too restrictive
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: Resource exhaustion manifests as OOMKilled pods, evictions, or throttling. Use metrics investigation to identify which resource is exhausted (memory, CPU, disk). Distinguish between insufficient limits (pod can't get enough) and excessive usage (application consuming too much). Check if the issue affects a single pod or multiple pods/nodes.
recommendations: Increase resource requests and limits based on actual usage patterns
Identify and fix memory leaks or CPU-intensive operations in application
Scale horizontally by adding more pod replicas
Add node capacity if cluster-wide resource exhaustion
Implement pod autoscaling (HPA) based on metrics
Add resource monitoring and alerts for early detection

patterns.name: Configuration Issues
investigation_steps: Check Pod events for specific error messages
Verify ConfigMap and Secret references exist
Check image pull credentials and registry accessibility
Verify volume mount paths and permissions
Look for recent ConfigMap or Secret changes
Check environment variable references
Verify command and args in Pod spec
Review application startup logs for configuration errors
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: Configuration issues prevent pods from starting successfully. CrashLoopBackOff indicates the container starts but fails immediately. ImagePullBackOff indicates image cannot be pulled. Check Pod events first for specific error messages. Verify all referenced resources (ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs) exist. Look for recent changes in deployment or configuration.
recommendations: Fix missing or incorrect ConfigMap/Secret references
Correct image pull credentials or image name
Fix volume mount paths or add missing volumes
Validate configuration syntax and required fields
Use init containers to validate configuration before main container starts
Implement configuration validation in CI/CD pipeline
Add monitoring for pod restart patterns

patterns.name: Routing and Gateway Issues
investigation_steps: Verify HTTPRoute or Route exists for the requested path
Check HTTPRoute/Route selector matches Gateway listener
Verify backend Service references are correct
Check Service exists and has healthy endpoints
For Istio: Verify VirtualService and Gateway configuration
For Istio: Check DestinationRule for backend availability
Look for conflicting routes or incorrect path matching
Verify TLS configuration if using HTTPS
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: Routing issues manifest as 404 errors or gateway timeouts when traffic cannot find a path to the backend. Verify the route configuration chain: Gateway → HTTPRoute → Service → Pods. Check for 'negative space' - what routes are MISSING that should exist. Ensure path matching rules are correct (exact, prefix, regex). Verify the Service has healthy endpoints.
recommendations: Create or fix HTTPRoute for the missing path
Correct HTTPRoute backend Service references
Fix Gateway listener configuration to match HTTPRoute
Adjust path matching rules to cover required paths
Ensure backend Service has healthy endpoints
Add monitoring for route coverage and 404 rates
Document route architecture and ownership

patterns.name: Cascading Failures
investigation_steps: Identify all failing services using FAILED_CALL_TO relationships
Traverse dependency chain to find the leaf service (original failure)

Filter failures by recency - compare failure timestamps with event timestamp. Only consider failures within 5-10 minutes of the triggering event. Older failures are likely stale/resolved unless continuously failing.
Verify if upstream services are propagating the failure or adding new errors
Distinguish between root cause (leaf) and symptoms (upstream failures)
Check if the root cause service has its own underlying issue
Assess blast radius using affected service count
Determine if circuit breakers or retries are amplifying the problem
patterns.diagnosis_guidance: Cascading failures occur when a single service failure propagates through the dependency chain, causing multiple services to fail. The key is identifying the leaf service (the original failure point) vs upstream services that are merely propagating errors. Look for the service with no failed dependencies but is itself failing. Check timestamps to determine which service failed first. Upstream services typically show 'downstream service unavailable' errors.
recommendations: Fix the root cause issue in the leaf service
Implement circuit breakers to prevent cascade amplification
Add timeout and retry policies with exponential backoff
Implement graceful degradation for non-critical dependencies
Add health checks and readiness probes
Monitor dependency health and implement alerts
Document service dependencies and criticality levels
